global_caption: The video contains 10 shots, depicting a large-scale cat choir performance set in a cold-toned, pixel-art style post-apocalyptic transit hub. The overall color palette features steel blue, gray-white, and muted teal-green, with lighting unified through overcast diffused cool light and broken neon backlighting. The camera movement progresses from reserved to solemn and uplifting, then gradually slows to a close. a slender shadow dares to cross the long night in pursuit of light. '
shot1: Shot 1 fades in from black, using a wide-angle overhead establishing shot. Composition uses cracks and abandoned tracks in the center of the ruined square as leading lines, with overturned signs and pixelated rubble in the foreground, and a collapsed station and fractured overpass in the background. The 24 cats are arranged in a tight rectangular formation at the center of the square. Cold fog drifts slowly across the ground, and a broken neon sign flickers faintly. Focus is centered on the formation. The camera slowly lowers and slightly pushes forward, establishing the wasteland space and collective ritualistic atmosphere.
shot2: Shot 2 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a medium-wide eye-level tracking shot. The camera moves through the collapsed station entrance, with hanging rebar and partially blocked ticket gates in the foreground, and two columns of cats advancing along cracked tiles in the background. The composition uses the station archway to create a frame-within-a-frame effect, with moderate depth of field and focus on the front of the formation. Cool diffused light continues to cover the space, while neon backlighting from the side-rear outlines silhouettes. As the cats' paws land, they crush small shards of glass, and their tails drag empty cans, producing brief metallic taps. The camera moves parallel to the direction of motion, shifting one frame per step in sync with the footfalls.
shot3: Shot 3 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a close-up low-angle shot focused on the lead cat standing on a damaged gate. Blurred iron bars in the foreground create a sense of pressure, while the dim waiting hall and tilted clock board appear in the background. The cat slowly lifts its head, ears perk up, whiskers tremble slightly, and chest rise is clearly visible. Its right paw gently taps a dented empty can beside it as a cue to start.
shot4: Shot 4 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a full-shot eye-level frontal composition. Two rows of cats are symmetrically arranged in the center of the collapsed station hall. The foreground features cold reflections on dusty ground, and the background includes shattered ticket windows and tilted light boxes. Cool lighting remains consistent, with occasional flickering neon creating pixelated halo effects along edges. The camera slightly pulls back to fully reveal the formation, transitioning the emotional tone from restraint to determination.
shot5: Shot 5 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a medium eye-level horizontal pan. Shattered glass and rolling empty cans in the foreground create dynamic obstructions. In the midground, more cats join the harmony. A broken wall gap and wind-blown old platform flags are visible in the background. Harmonic thickness increases noticeably. The camera rapidly pans along the formation, moving at a speed perfectly matched to the harmonic expansion.
shot6: Shot 6 matches action with an upward cut from the previous shot, using a full-shot high-angle view. The camera rises from a broken station sign on the ground to the roof of a derelict bus. Rusty handrails appear in the foreground, and a broken bridge and gray sky in the background. The composition creates a two-tiered choral space. The bus roof vibrates slightly with each step, and metal resonance combined with repeated echoes of distant automatic doors forms new rhythmic points.
shot7: Shot 7 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a close-up eye-level shot. Focus is locked on a row of cats' whiskers, nose tips, and mouths. Cool light traces fine contours along facial edges.
shot8: Shot 8 hard cuts from the previous shot, using a wide-angle overhead shot. The 24 cats form a semi-circular formation on cracked ground in the waiting hall. A broken clock outer ring appears in the foreground, and cold daylight filters through a wall breach in the background. Empty cans used as percussion instruments are scattered around the edge of the formation. The composition has strong geometric structure, with focus covering the entire semi-circle. As they reach the first half of "也敢穿过长夜追光", a partially broken side door is blown open by the wind, and the echoing door The camera slowly rotates clockwise in a slight overhead arc, reinforcing the group choreography.
shot9: Shot 9 fades in from the previous shot to intensify emotion, using a medium-close low-angle shot. The camera is positioned low in front of the semi-circular cat group. Cracked platform edges appear in the foreground, and a broken neon sign and collapsed roof in the background. All cats raise their heads collectively, chests expand, tails and shoulder lines forming an upward force. Cold neon lights flash more prominently at the climax, but the overall tone remains consistently cool. A heavy iron door thuds once at the end of the phrase. The camera quickly pushes in and slightly tilts upward, amplifying the power of the climax to its peak.
shot10: Shot 10 hard cuts from the previous shot and slowly concludes, using a wide-angle eye-level pull-out. The frame returns to the main transit hub space beneath the broken neon sign. A slightly swaying iron door appears in the foreground, the 24 cats remain in formation but gradually relax their posture in the midground, and an empty platform and cold fog appear in the background. The composition places the neon sign above, creating a looming sense of pressure.
